main_body: Flat snow ground patch (4x3 tiles) with pale blue-white snow areas and dark grey-green speckled patches, repeating as a tiled stamp
top_band: none; this is a flat terrain surface, not a standing object, so there is no top/front split to read
evidence: Terrain ground tile with no vertical faces. The 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply, and no wrong-projection structure (front elevation, rim only, side elevation, slab) is drawn.

style.evidence: The dark patches are well textured, with about 4 grey-green steps and scattered speckle. The snow lobes are large areas of one pale tone with only 2-3 steps and no grain or per-clump variation, so they read as flat fills (some are about 8x5 px or larger). The whole 32px motif repeats identically and looks like a stamped pattern, not a naturally varied ground. Snow tiles carry only about 2-4 colours each, which pulls the median per-tile density below the reference. There are no outlines, which is acceptable for ground. Overall it is thinner than the Beodeul reference in the snow areas.
